title: Scope and applicable regime
notes: Decide first whether the federal law, a free-zone regime (DIFC, ADGM) or a sector law applies

title: Lawful basis and consent
notes: Processing without consent (Art. 4) and conditions for valid consent (Art. 6)

title: Processing principles (purpose, minimisation, accuracy, retention)
notes: Retention and deletion evidence usually comes from A.8.10

title: Controller and processor obligations
notes: Includes choosing processors with sufficient guarantees and processing per instructions

title: Record of personal data processing
notes: Controller and processor each keep a record; extend the A.5.9 inventory with processing details

title: Security of processing
notes: Technical and organisational measures; the ISMS supplies most of the evidence

title: Personal data breach notification
notes: Notify the regulator and affected data subjects; timelines and form depend on the Executive Regulations

title: Data protection officer
notes: Appointment and duties of the DPO and the support owed to the DPO

title: Data subject rights
articles: Art. 13; Art. 14; Art. 15; Art. 16; Art. 17; Art. 18; Art. 19
notes: Information, portability, correction or erasure, restriction, stopping processing and automated processing; ISO 27001 has no rights-handling control

title: Data protection impact assessment
notes: Required before high-risk processing using new technologies (for example profiling or large volumes of sensitive data)

title: Cross-border transfer
notes: Transfers with and without an adequate level of protection; cloud hosting location matters

title: Complaints and regulator cooperation
notes: Data subjects can complain to the regulator; keep regulator contacts current
